parole.significato: -ory; suffix attached to the supine stem of Latin verbs to form adjectives
parole.testo: Calque of Latin -ōrius (“-ory”) (itself from -ōr + -ius), using -or (from Latin -ōr) + -isch (from Proto-Germanic *-iskaz).

From Middle High German hērre, hërre, from Old High German hēriro, hērro, originally comparative of hēr (“grey-haired, noble, venerable”, whence German hehr), a semantic loan from Latin senior (“elder”). Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *hairaz (“grey”). Cognate with Dutch heer, Old English hār, Engli

parole.significato: habit (a long piece of clothing worn by monks and nuns)
parole.testo: From Middle High German kutte (“monk habit”), from Medieval Latin cotta (“undercoat, tunic”), from Proto-Germanic *kuttô (“cowl, woolen cloth, coat”).
Middle High German pedel, from Medieval Latin pedellus, bedellus, perhaps influenced by Büttel, from Proto-Germanic *budilaz. Cognate with English bedel and beadle.
